perspective:
Christian Mensah’s accessible information:

- He knows Jonathan as a childhood friend/best friend, often seeks his advice, and values his perspective.
- He felt anxious and suspicious that Jonathan was hiding something important because Jonathan had been acting differently.
- He arranged and attended a meeting with Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop to confront him.
- Jonathan told him he could trust him, then admitted he had been keeping something from Christian: Jonathan is in trouble and didn’t know how to tell him.
- Christian offered to help. Jonathan said the situation is complicated, didn’t want to drag Christian into it, but could use support and resources to get out of the mess.
- Christian suspected/asked whether the trouble was related to illegal activity. Jonathan said he couldn’t say for sure, might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but claimed he didn’t do anything illegal himself.
- Christian told Jonathan he would look into the matter discreetly. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Through his own investigation, Christian came to believe/learned that Jonathan is being framed and that someone is trying to set him up. He had leads but not all the facts, and decided to gather more evidence to prove Jonathan’s innocence.
- Christian later found out who is behind it and told Jonathan it is someone both of them know and trust. He felt betrayed and resolved to confront this person and bring them to justice.
- Jonathan warned Christian to be careful because the person is dangerous, and said he trusted Christian.
